THE DECISION

Start with delivery reliability.

Late deliveries are a minority of orders, but their review scores are much lower. The first operational review should combine the number of late orders with the late rate, rather than ranking destinations on one metric alone.

On-time orders average 4.29/5; late orders average 2.27/5.
This is a descriptive relationship. Product mix, location, seller performance and review selection can also affect the comparison.

Commercial scope: delivered orders across the extract. Currency: Brazilian real (BRL). Product sales represent item price, not marketplace revenue or profit. No performance claim is made about Olist today.

01 / COMMERCIAL PERFORMANCE

Establish the sales baseline.

Delivered orders generated R$ 13,221,498.11 in product sales, with a product-only average order value of R$ 137.04. The highest sales month in the displayed window is 2017-11; the data alone do not explain why.

Grouped by purchase month, not delivery month. Sparse 2016 edge months are omitted from this chart but retained in total sales. August 2018 can be affected by the closing observation window.

Category totals use item prices only. An order can contain several categories, so category order counts cannot be added together.

02 / DELIVERY AND EXPERIENCE

Balance exposure with service risk.

SP accounts for 1,820 late orders, the largest count, at a 4.49% late rate. The destinations below are the eight largest late-order counts among states with at least 100 eligible deliveries.

Low reviews are 6.7 times as common among late orders.
The 1–2 star rate is 62.4% for late orders and 9.3% for on-time orders: a 53.2 percentage-point gap.

Low score = 1 or 2 stars. Eligible deliveries with a valid selected review only. Wilson intervals describe binomial uncertainty under independence assumptions; repeated customers and shared sellers may violate independence. They do not address confounding or review nonresponse. Earliest/latest review-policy comparisons are included in the output tables.

03 / CUSTOMER DEPTH · OPTIONAL ADVANCED ANALYSIS

Measure repeat purchasing with fair follow-up.

2,801 of 93,358 observed customers placed more than one delivered order (3.00%). The cohort view gives each purchase group its own follow-up timeline.

Rows are first observed delivered-purchase months. A customer is counted once in each later month with a delivered purchase. Rates are not cumulative; the same customer may return in several months. Month 0 is 100% by definition and omitted. Grey cells are unobserved, not zero. Cutoff: 31 July 2018.

Use this to design a repeat-purchase pilot, not to label all one-time customers as churned. The marketplace extract has a limited window and does not capture a customer's purchases outside the dataset.

04 / SELLER CONCENTRATION

Prioritise service coverage where sales are concentrated.

The top 20% of delivered-order sellers account for 82.3% of product sales. Reviewing service coverage for this group is a practical starting point. An order's delivery outcome can be shared by multiple sellers, so the analysis cannot identify who caused a delay.

NEXT ACTIONS

Turn findings into testable work.

Operations

Review handoff, transit and promised dates in the largest late-order destinations. Track both late-order volume and rate weekly before assigning responsibility.

Customer experience

Trial proactive updates for at-risk orders. Use a controlled pilot to measure the change in low-review rates.

Seller management

Review service coverage for high-sales sellers. Use the exported seller table for investigation, with a minimum eligible-order threshold when comparing rates.

Customer marketing

Test a repeat-purchase offer with equal follow-up windows and a control group. Compare incremental repeat purchasing rather than raw campaign totals.

These are proposed actions. The project does not claim realised savings, profit growth or an intervention effect.

METHOD AND QUALITY

Keep the numbers traceable.

  • Order items and payments are aggregated separately before joining. Order totals are never repeated across item rows.
  • The latest answered review is selected per order; ties use creation timestamp and review ID. A second selection policy is exported for comparison.
  • Same-calendar-day arrivals count as on time. 8 delivered orders have unusable delivery dates and are excluded from service-rate denominators.
  • One delivered order lacks a payment record. 256 delivered orders have a payment difference above R$0.05 versus item prices plus freight. Original values are preserved and the two monetary measures remain separate.
  • The geolocation file is profiled but not joined: it has multiple records per ZIP prefix, and state-level analysis already answers the business question.
  • Costs, refund-ledger entries, carrier identity and experiment assignment are unavailable. No margin or causal estimate is presented.

10 reconciliation checks passed. The project includes source-file hashes, missing-value counts, quality diagnostics, exported summary tables and synthetic edge-case tests.

All purchase timestamps span 2016-09-04 to 2018-10-17; delivered purchases span 2016-09-15 to 2018-08-29. Timestamps are analysed as supplied, without an assumed timezone conversion.
